This project utilized k-means clustering to group MLB players by their two-strike approaches. MLB Savant released new bat tracking data for the 2024 season, like bat speed and swing length, which makes this project possible. It's a common belief to take a two-strike approach (prioritizing contact and reducing bat speed) in baseball, but is this true in the MLB?

For clustering, I selected three variables: bat speed, two-strike xWOBA, and strikeout percentage. Using the elbow method, I found that 5 clusters was ideal. At the bottom of the poster, I also included median statistical measures for each cluster, adding in swing length and barrel percentage. Overall, the model segmented two-strike hitters into five groups: poor, power, contact, better contact, and average two-strike hitters. Pitchers can take this analysis and better plan when facing certain batters, based on their two-strike hitting abilities.

I presented this project at the 5th Annual Ohio State Sports Analytics Conference and won the award for “Outstanding Sports Analytics for Professional Sports.” The poster is attached.
